nodes.title: Item No. 4
nodes.summary: This explanatory statement under Section 102 of the Companies Act, 2013, concerns Item No. 4 of the AGM notice: ratification of remuneration payable to the Cost Auditor under Section 148. It details the appointment of M/s. Ramanath Iyer & Co., a cost accounting firm, as Cost Auditor for FY 2025-26 at a remuneration of ₹2,40,000 plus expenses and taxes, same as last year. The firm's background, expertise, team, and clientele are described. The Board approved the appointment on the Audit Committee's recommendation, deeming the remuneration fair and reasonable. The firm's written consent, eligibility confirmation, and absence of disqualifications or pending proceedings are noted. No directors or key managerial personnel are interested in the resolution, and the Board recommends approval via Ordinary Resolution.

nodes.title: Item No. 5

It outlines his initial appointment, roles (Lead Independent Director, Committee Chairman/Member), qualifications, expertise, and contributions. It covers his attendance, remuneration (sitting fees and commission), other directorships and committee memberships, and a past resignation. It includes his consent, confirmations of independence and eligibility, and compliance with regulations. The Board recommends re-appointment based on NRC recommendation and performance, subject to shareholder approval via Special Resolution. It notes inspection of the re-appointment letter, interests of directors/KMP, and regulatory disclosures.

nodes.title: Item No. 6

It covers his nomination by Nestlé S.A., transition plan including his joining as Managing Director (Designate) and Key Managerial Personnel, and his professional background. It outlines proposed remuneration terms—salary, allowances, commission, performance-linked incentives, long-term incentive loss compensation, perquisites with ceilings, minimum remuneration, and other terms like termination notice—and seeks member approval via Ordinary Resolution at the 66th AGM. It also notes his consent, disqualification declarations, shareholding, prior remuneration, a lump sum joining payout with reimbursement clause, and inspection details, recommending his appointment in the Company's interest.

nodes.title: Item No. 7

nodes.title: COMMUNICATION ON TAX DEDUCTED AT SOURCE (TDS) ON DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION
nodes.summary: The section outlines TDS provisions on dividend distribution under the Income Tax Act, 1961, requiring members to update details like PAN, residential status, and category by the Record Date of 4th July 2025. It details TDS rates and required documents for resident members, including exemptions for specific entities and conditions for lower/no TDS, and for non-resident members, covering beneficial rates, DTAA benefits, and documentation. It also provides general information on surcharge rates, TDS certificates, refunds, indemnity, and a note advising members to consult tax advisors, along with an Annexure A for self-declaration.

nodes.title: Section 1: For all members - Details that should be completed and /or updated, as applicable
nodes.summary: The text communicates TDS provisions on dividend distribution under the Income Tax Act, 1961, stating dividend is taxable for members and the Company must deduct TDS at prescribed rates. It requests all members to update details in their demat accounts or with the Company by the Record Date of 4th July 2025, which will be relied upon for TDS compliance. Required details include valid PAN, residential status for FY 2025-26, member category (listing various categories like Mutual Fund, Insurance Company, AIF, Government, FPI/FII, Individual, HUF, Firm, LLP, AOP/BOI/AJP, Trust, Domestic/Foreign Company), email address, and address.

nodes.title: Section 2: TDS provisions and documents required, as applicable for relevant category of members Members are requested to take note of the TDS rates and document(s), if any, required to be submitted to the Company by the Record Date their respective category, in order to comply with the applicable TDS provisions. I. For Resident members:
nodes.summary: Section 2 covers TDS provisions and required documents for resident members, detailing exemptions for mutual funds, insurance companies, Category I/II AIFs, recognized provident funds, approved superannuation funds, approved gratuity funds, National Pension Scheme, government entities, and any other exempt entities. It specifies applicable IT Act sections or circulars for each category and the self-attested documents needed, such as SEBI/IRDA registration certificates, Commissioner orders, or other valid evidence, to comply with TDS provisions by the Record Date.

nodes.title: x. Other resident members:
nodes.summary: This text outlines TDS rules for resident members' dividends: 10% deduction under section 194; no TDS if aggregate dividend is up to ₹10,000 based on preceding year's dividend; exemption via valid Form 15G/15H with mandatory fields and company discretion, requiring fresh declarations for subsequent tranches if changes occur; mandatory valid PAN; higher TDS at 20% under section 206AA for PAN not linked with Aadhaar per section 139AA effective July 1, 2023; and lower TDS if a valid certificate under section 197 is provided.

nodes.title: II. For Non-resident members:

i. Any entity entitled to beneficial rate / exemption from TDS: Valid self-attested documentary evidence (e.g. relevant copy of registration, notification, order, etc. by Indian tax authorities) in support of the entity being entitled to beneficial rate / exemption from TDS needs to be submitted.

nodes.title: Other non-resident members:
nodes.summary: The text outlines TDS rules for non-resident members: 20% TDS under sections 196D (FPI/FII) or 195 (other non-residents), plus surcharge and cess. Lower TDS under DTAA requires submitting a self-attested PAN (or Rule 37BC details), valid TRC, Form 10F (electronic per CBDT notification 03/2022), and a self-declaration on letterhead confirming no Permanent Establishment, beneficial ownership, and treaty eligibility (Annexure A). Alternatively, a valid section 197 lower withholding certificate applies. Members must email completed, signed documents with PAN in the subject to investor@in.nestle.com by the Record Date; no late submissions are accepted. The company is not obligated to apply DTAA rates; this depends on complete, satisfactory document review.

nodes.title: Section 3: Other general information for the members:
nodes.summary: The text outlines general information for members regarding document certification, TDS deduction based on registered member details, and TDS certificates. It details surcharge rates for non-residents for FY 2025-26 across different entity types, the basis for surcharge determination, and health and education cess. It addresses multiple accounts with a single PAN, shares transferred to IEPF, TDS rate application with due diligence, and the option to claim refunds. It covers past withholding tax adjustments, income tax rates under the latest Finance Act, and the new tax regime default option with opt-out procedure. Finally, it includes an indemnity clause for tax demands arising from misrepresentation.

structure.title: NESPRESSO
structure.summary: Nespresso opened its first boutique at Select Citywalk Mall, New Delhi, marking a milestone in its global expansion after entering India in late 2024. It introduced best-selling coffees and machines from Original and Professional ranges, plus milk-based solutions for Indian preferences. structure.title: Sales
key_items: NesMitra; Re-Distributor 'Distributor Management Solution' RD DMS
structure.summary: The text covers the Company's sales strategy, focusing on an omni-channel approach. It details the RUrban strategy with five pillars (infrastructure, product portfolio, technology, visibility, consumer connect), highlighting a 7.5% increase in total reach, expansion from 20,783 to 28,240 distribution touchpoints, presence in 209,050 villages, smart stores, haat activities, and Project Swabhimaan adding 250 women entrepreneurs (cumulative 2,100). Technology interventions include RD DMS for automating sub-distributors. E-commerce grew, driven by quick commerce (45% of e-commerce business, 8.6% of sales), with campaigns like NESCAFÉ Ready-to-Drink cold coffee. Sushrut Nallulwar's quote emphasizes reach expansion and omnichannel commitment. Technology integration includes NesMitra (70% wholesale hub business), RD DMS (re-distributors ~50% of RUrban business), and RACE for trade activity automation.

structure.title: Where the Best of Science and Quality Converge
structure.summary: The text covers Nestlé India's Milk Products and Nutrition performance. It highlights MILKMAID's 37.9% contribution to sales and 34 million tins sold, the launch of MILKMAID Mini in a resealable doy format exceeding 1,000 tons, and innovative dessert applications. NESCAFÉ RTD's growth and new café-style cold coffee range (Iced Latte, Iced Frappe at INR 50; Choco, Caramel, Classic Latte at INR 75) achieving market leadership. Nestlé a+ launched unsweetened low-fat Greek yoghurt with 10% daily protein. Nutrition business emphasizes breastfeeding, launched zero refined sugar CERELAC and CEREGROW cereals, and NANGROW's '7 Signs of Growth'. Quotes from Manav Sahni and Vineet Singh stress quality, sustainability, and science-based innovation including 5 HMOs.

It highlights MAGGI's 50-year anniversary, innovation and renovation (Spicy Cheesy variant, affordable Nutrilicious Veg Atta noodles, Korean range, and category-first MAGGI Besan Noodles), and a 40% plastic reduction in Cuppa noodles. Campaigns include 'Rishtey Maangein bas 2 minute' for togetherness and 'Banaye roz ka khana kaamal' for Masala-e-Magic. Digitalization and e-commerce efforts drove Q-commerce growth, and sustainability includes reduced plastic and recyclable packaging. A quote from Rupali Rattan emphasizes focusing on the core while accelerating innovations and deepening consumer trust.

structure.title: Beginning Every Day with Crunchy-Munchy Goodness

The launch of MUNCH CHOCO FILLS, combining whole wheat, rice, and corn crunch with a chocolate filling, is detailed. It reports a 13.8% contribution to total sales and 12.1 billion cups sold, with quotes from Sunayan Mitra on double-digit growth and market leadership. NESCAFÉ in-home portfolio (CLASSIC, Sunrise, GOLD) achieved double-digit growth, highest household penetration, and market share gains. NESCAFÉ CLASSIC led youth recruitment with a renovated product, refreshed identity, and 'Make Your World' campaign. NESCAFÉ SUNRISE succeeded in South India with a renovated product and cluster strategy, while NESCAFÉ GOLD drove premium coffee growth. Innovations include NESCAFÉ ICE ROAST for cold coffee and NESCAFÉ ROASTERY for luxury. Sustainability efforts feature value chain enhancements to alleviate inflation, farmer partnerships in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala via the NESCAFÉ Plan, and International Coffee Day farmer story packaging.

nodes.title: Nestlé India FY2025: Exports, Business Development, and Nutrition Portfolio
nodes.summary: The page covers Nestlé India's FY2025 performance across three sections. Exports expanded to Maldives and Papua New Guinea with confectionery, and introduced MAGGI noodles in the Middle East and South Africa, plus NESTLÉ MUNCH, NESCAFÉ SUNRISE, and MAGGI Masala-Ae-Magic in the US and UAE. Milk Products and Nutrition saw new CERELAC and CEREGROW variants with no refined sugar. Petcare achieved highest-ever growth; OOH strong double-digit; NESPRESSO boutique opened. E-commerce contributed 8.5% of domestic sales; RUrban strategy and ₹65,000 million investment noted, including Odisha factory. nodes.title: Indian Economy
nodes.summary: India's economic growth is projected at 6.4% real GDP in FY25, with strong aggregate demand driven by a 7.3% rise in private consumption due to rural demand rebound and agriculture recovery at 3.8%. However, sluggish manufacturing growth challenges job creation and global manufacturing hub ambitions, requiring targeted policy interventions for unemployment and demographic dividend. Economic momentum relies on domestic consumption and government spending, cushioning international volatility. Headline inflation fell to a seven-month low of 3.6% in February 2025, especially in food, expected to boost purchasing power and sustain demand.

nodes.title: FMCG Sector: Navigating Change and Seizing Opportunities
nodes.summary: The text covers India's FMCG sector as the fourth-largest, contributing 3% to GDP and employing 3 million, with 2024 challenges from inflation and shifting consumption. It highlights quick commerce's rise, with 31% of urban Indians using it for primary grocery shopping and 39% for top-ups. Brands are adopting premiumization, value-driven strategies, and nutrition-focused innovation like millet-based and fortified foods, plus plant-based proteins and healthy aging products. Sustainability is crucial, with consumers favoring responsible brands. India's consumer landscape includes 496 million consumers (35% urban, 65% rural), five generations, Gen Z and Millennials driving trends, and a growing elderly population (over 10% now, one in five by 2050). AI and Gen AI are reshaping the sector, with India contributing 16% to the global AI workforce, enhancing analytics across sourcing, engagement, supply chain, and personalization.
